stem: What distinguishes Pulmonary Interstitial Emphysema (PIE) on a neonatal X-ray?

options.text: A sharp, clear plural line with no lung markings beyond it.
Radiating bubbly lucencies extending from the hilum into the supporting lung structures.
A uniform triangular density suggesting lobar collapse.
The appearance of 'angel wings' due to air in the pericardium.

explanation: PIE is a complication of positive pressure ventilation where air leaks into the interstitial supporting structures of the lung.
rationale: Focus on the pattern of air trapped within the tissue that supports the airways.

optionExplanations.A: This describes a pneumothorax, not interstitial emphysema.
optionExplanations.B: PIE is a complication of positive pressure ventilation where air leaks into the interstitial supporting structures of the lung.
optionExplanations.C: Uniform triangular densities are characteristic of atelectasis (collapse), not PIE.
optionExplanations.D: Angel wings refer to pneumomediastinum affecting the thymus; air in the pericardium is pneumopericardium.

source.hint: Focus on the pattern of air trapped within the tissue that supports the airways.
